source.title: Orthogonal Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: K. Jia; Shuai Li; Yu-Xin Wen; Tong-Liang Liu; D. Tao

record.file_problem: none; the complete paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether spectral weight regularization changes image-classification generalization, using methods not covered by the listed versions.
record.gate_note: Own image-classification error comparisons for OrthDNN methods are included. Cited results about random-label fitting and other papers' results are not rows. Training error and generalization gap are not reported as paired measurements.
record.test_reason: The study reports spectral-regularization performance and derives a singular-value-based generalization bound; neither tests V1–V8. Its discussion of random-label memorization and sharp minima relies on prior work. Orthogonality regularization is neither dropout nor magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors derive a generalization bound whose isometry-dependent component is minimized by equal singular values within each layer, motivate OrthDNNs, and report classification and corruption-robustness gains from their methods. This does not establish an empirical sharpness–gap correlation, and Table 2 shows that BBN does not improve every regularizer.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares spectral orthogonality regularizers (strict manifold constraints, soft regularization, SRIP, SVB) and BBN against SGD-based baselines; it does not reproduce the listed versions' interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with architecture, dataset, regularization method, and normalization choice (BN, BBN, or DBN); gains are reported as more obvious on smaller ImageNet training subsets.

fits_no_version.finding: Orthogonality regularization reduces reported classification error against the SGD baselines in Tables 1–4; for example, ConvNet error falls from 16.68% to 10.39% with soft regularization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral orthogonality regularization can improve held-out image-classification performance under the tested training recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: BBN improves SVB's mean error from 5.96% to 5.88%, but increases soft-regularization error from 6.28% to 6.30% and SRIP error from 5.95% to 6.10%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of bounded batch normalization depends on the accompanying orthogonality regularizer.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.4 reports improvement across four ImageNet training-subset sizes, with larger gains for smaller subsets; exact gains are figure-only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SVB and BBN can improve ResNeXt-101 classification across the tested sample sizes, especially smaller ones.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.5 reports improved ResNeXt-101 performance on ImageNet-C across corruption severities; exact gains are figure-only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral orthogonality regularization can improve robustness to common image corruptions.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
record.problems: The reported classification error comparisons do not provide paired training errors or a training–test gap measurement. Several additional improvements are presented only in figures without numerical values in the text. Table 1 gives no run variability; Table 2 reports five runs.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible reported results left out. The paper's validation curves in Figure 3 and exact plotted improvements in Figures 4–5 are not transcribed where the text gives no values; Figure 3 shows convergence but no separate numeric results are stated.

untested.parts: Own measurements of random-label fitting and chance-level held-out accuracy alongside natural-label generalization under the same recipe.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of learned local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations. Section 5.3 changes epochs and batch size together and supplies no controlled batch-size comparison.
Dropout addition, removal, strength, and interaction with training-set size or augmentation.

Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, measured training–test gaps, and comparative ranking against norm or margin measures. Singular-value bounds and input-corruption robustness do not measure these.
Removal of examples selected by label-memorization influence versus equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain outside V1–V8. Their cannot_determine states concern those versions, not whether the reported classification improvements occurred. The comparisons are useful for a separate spectral-regularization claim but are not eligible evidence for the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out behavior on natural labels are not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
The study tests orthogonality regularization, not dropout.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other measure of the training–test gap.
